Contributing to AudiomothR

Source: .github/CONTRIBUTING.md

Thank you for your interest in AudiomothR. Comments, questions, bug reports and improvements are welcome, from users of every level: you do not need to write code to help.

Asking a question or reporting a problem

Open an issue and choose the template that fits. For a problem, please include:

  • what you ran (the R code) and the full message you got;
  • the output of AudiomothR::check_requirements() and of sessionInfo();
  • if the problem comes from a card, its CONFIG.TXT and the names of a few WAV files. Please do not attach real recordings or exact locations of sensitive species: the example card of the package (system.file("extdata", "example", "card", package = "AudiomothR")) is often enough to reproduce a problem.

Issues may be written in English or Spanish.

Proposing a change

Small fixes (typos, documentation) can go directly as a pull request. For anything bigger, please open an issue first, so that we can agree on the design before you spend time on it.

  1. Fork the repository and create a branch from main.
  2. Install the development dependencies: install.packages(c("devtools", "testthat", "knitr", "rmarkdown")).
  3. Make your change, with tests in tests/testthat/ when it changes what a function does.
  4. Update the documentation with devtools::document() and check the package with devtools::check(): it should give 0 errors, 0 warnings and 0 notes.
  5. Add a line to NEWS.md, at the top, describing the change for users.
  6. Open the pull request, describing what it changes and why.

Conventions of the code

  • The whole package is in English: function and argument names, messages, comments, documentation and vignettes.
  • R code must be ASCII: write non-ASCII characters in strings as \uxxxx escapes (comments and roxygen may have accents).
  • Messages with cli through the internal helpers inform() (it respects options(AudiomothR.quiet = TRUE)) and abort().
  • External programs (ffmpeg, Quarto) are always run with processx::run(), with the arguments as a vector.
  • Documentation with roxygen2 in markdown; do not edit the files in man/ by hand.
  • Tests use testthat 3 and a synthetic card (tests/testthat/helper-card.R); BirdNET and GBIF are mocked, so the tests run without Python or Internet.

Code of conduct

Please note that AudiomothR is released with a Contributor Code of Conduct. By contributing to this project you agree to abide by its terms.
